claims.claim: Jobs support email_notifications and webhook_notifications with on_start, on_success and on_failure; job-level notifications are not sent when failed tasks are retried; at most 3 destinations per on_failure.
Databricks SQL alerts run a query on a schedule and notify when a condition is met.

concept_html:
An alert is useful when it fires for real problems, reaches the person who can act, and says enough to start. Pipelines need two kinds.

1. Loud failures: the job fails. Databricks job notifications send an email or a webhook message when a run fails. In a job definition or bundle:

email_notifications:
  on_failure:
    - data-oncall@example.org

These fire only if the job actually fails. Every except block that logs and carries on silences them. Log, record the run as FAILED, then re-raise (lesson A7-L2).

Job-level notifications are not sent when a failed task is retried. If you want a message for every failed attempt, add task-level notifications.

2. Silent failures: the job succeeds, but the data is wrong or missing. A job that never starts, a MERGE that writes 0 rows, a wave with a WARN on every contract check. No job fails, so no notification fires. Detect these with queries on your run log and QA results tables, run on a schedule, for example as Databricks SQL alerts:

  • No SUCCESS run for a pipeline in the last 26 hours (a daily job plus slack).
  • A run with rows_processed = 0.
  • More WARN results for a wave than the last five waves' average.

Write each alert query against the exact values your tables hold. A query for status = 'FAIL' never fires on a table that stores FAILED.

Send alerts to a group address or channel, never to one person's inbox. Include the pipeline, the wave, the run ID and a link, so the reader can start without searching.

lines: -- Alert 1: pipelines with no successful run in the last 26 hours.
max(finished_at) AS last_success
FROM research_prod.research_governance.pipeline_run_log
WHERE status = 'SUCCESS'
HAVING max(finished_at) < current_timestamp() - INTERVAL 26 HOURS;
-- Alert 2: successful runs that wrote nothing in the last day.
SELECT pipeline_name, wave_id, run_id
FROM research_prod.research_governance.pipeline_run_log
WHERE status = 'SUCCESS'
AND rows_processed = 0
AND finished_at >= current_timestamp() - INTERVAL 1 DAY;

A success that did nothing is a silent failure worth an alert.

exercises.solution:
from datetime import datetime, timedelta


def stale_pipelines(runs: list[dict[str, object]], now: datetime, max_age_hours: int = 26) -> list[str]:
    """Pipelines whose latest SUCCESS is older than max_age_hours, or that never succeeded.

    Args:
        runs: Run log rows with pipeline_name, status and finished_at.
        now: Current time, timezone-aware.
        max_age_hours: Largest acceptable age of the latest success.

    Returns:
        Sorted pipeline names.
    """
    cutoff = now - timedelta(hours=max_age_hours)
    latest: dict[str, datetime | None] = {}
    for r in runs:
        name = str(r["pipeline_name"])
        latest.setdefault(name, None)
        finished = r["finished_at"]
        if r["status"] == "SUCCESS" and isinstance(finished, datetime):
            current = latest[name]
            if current is None or finished > current:
                latest[name] = finished
    return sorted(name for name, last in latest.items() if last is None or last < cutoff)

def stale_pipelines(runs: list[dict[str, object]], now: datetime, max_age_hours: int = 26) -> list[str]:
"""Pipelines whose latest SUCCESS is older than max_age_hours, or that never succeeded.
Args:
runs: Run log rows with pipeline_name, status and finished_at.
now: Current time, timezone-aware.
max_age_hours: Largest acceptable age of the latest success.
Returns:
Sorted pipeline names.
"""
cutoff = now - timedelta(hours=max_age_hours)
latest: dict[str, datetime | None] = {}
for r in runs:
name = str(r["pipeline_name"])
latest.setdefault(name, None)
finished = r["finished_at"]
if r["status"] == "SUCCESS" and isinstance(finished, datetime):
current = latest[name]
if current is None or finished > current:
latest[name] = finished
return sorted(name for name, last in latest.items() if last is None or last < cutoff)

title: Alert on failures, and on the silence that hides them
why_html:
A nightly bronze job's schedule is paused during a workspace migration and never resumed. The job does not fail, because it never runs, so no failure email arrives. Silver and gold keep succeeding on the old data. Eleven days later a client asks why the dashboard has not moved.

A scheduled query, "no SUCCESS for nat_bronze_pipeline in 26 hours", would have alerted the on-call group on the second morning.
